answer: Latency-Skew Enrollment Window: each identity must submit requests spread across a randomized window with fixed minimum gaps, and its first activity must trail a walnut-seeded challenge by a nonce delay. A per-identity timing profile is checked against the observed envelope; automation that fires uniformly is flagged. Each slot also demands a small proof-of-work over a basalt-derived seed. Attacker cost is linear: N identities require N sustained timing profiles and N work proofs, so mass creation becomes wall-clock bound rather than fee bound. A timber-style rate cap trims burst enrollment.
